rounds.fact: Nintendo's site in the early 2000s was promoting both the GameCube and Game Boy Advance simultaneously, an unusually broad two-console push even by Nintendo's standards.
PerezHilton.com became one of the first hugely popular celebrity gossip blogs, known for its crude photo scribbles added directly on top of paparazzi pictures.
Netscape's browser dominated the early web so completely that Microsoft bundling Internet Explorer with Windows to compete became the center of a landmark antitrust case.
Bebo was massively popular in the UK and Ireland during the mid-2000s, at one point ranking as the third-most-visited social network in the US before AOL bought it for $850 million in 2008.
GameSpot launched in 1996 and became known for its numerical review scores becoming a genuine influence on game sales, sometimes controversially so.
